issues.legal_issue: The Supreme Court may determine the statutory limits and jurisdiction of a tribunal even when it cannot decide the merits of the inter-state water dispute assigned to that tribunal.
material_facts: The appeals challenged the tribunal’s refusal to entertain interim-relief applications on the ground that the applications were outside its jurisdiction.
The appellants asked the Supreme Court to determine the tribunal’s authority, not to decide the merits of the water dispute pending before it.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court had jurisdiction and an obligation to determine the scope and limits of the tribunal’s authority under its governing statute.
issues.legal_principle: The judiciary authoritatively interprets statutes and determines the jurisdictional boundaries of statutory bodies. The Court relied on Sanjeev Coke Manufacturing Company v. Bharat Coking Coal Ltd. and Kehar Singh v. Union of India, and referred to Tamil Nadu Cauvery Neerppasana Vilaiporulgal Vivasayigal Nala Urimal Padhugappu Sangam v. Union of India.

predicates.appeal_from_tribunal_jurisdiction_order: A party appealed an order in which a statutory tribunal declined to act because it considered itself outside its authority.
predicates.challenge_concerns_tribunal_authority_no: The challenge asks whether the tribunal’s governing law gives it the authority at issue, rather than asking the court to decide the underlying inter-state water dispute.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a statutory tribunal’s understanding of its authority without seeking a decision on the underlying dispute’s merits, the Supreme Court may determine the tribunal’s jurisdiction.

issues.legal_issue: The Supreme Court cannot decide the merits of an inter-state water dispute that has been referred to a tribunal under the statutory scheme.
material_facts: The dispute concerning the use, distribution, and control of the waters of an inter-state river had been referred to a tribunal and remained pending there.
The appellants sought interim relief from the tribunal, while these appeals challenged the tribunal’s refusal to entertain their applications.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court had no jurisdiction to decide the merits of the water dispute pending before the tribunal.
issues.legal_principle: Article 262 of the Constitution permits Parliament to exclude the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court and other courts over inter-state water disputes. Section 11 of the Inter-State Water Disputes Act, 1956, excludes court jurisdiction over water disputes that may be referred to a tribunal under the Act.

predicates.inter_state_water_dispute_proceeding: The proceeding concerns a dispute over the use, distribution, or control of the waters of an inter-state river or river valley.
predicates.supreme_court_asked_to_decide_referred_d: A party asks the Supreme Court to decide the merits of a water dispute that has been referred to a tribunal.

issues.definition: When a proceeding concerns an inter-state water dispute referred to a tribunal and asks the Supreme Court to decide its merits, the Supreme Court lacks jurisdiction to do so.

issues.legal_issue: Interim-relief applications fall within a reference when the reference encompasses the disputes emerging from a complaint that sought immediate relief.
material_facts: The central government referred the water disputes emerging from a state’s complaint to the tribunal.
The complaint described an urgent need for relief and injury caused by delay, including reduced water availability and harm to existing irrigation.
The tribunal dismissed interim-relief applications on the ground that the requested relief had not been referred to it.
issues.conclusion: The applications fell within the dispute referred to the tribunal, and the tribunal was directed to decide them on their merits.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 5 of the Inter-State Water Disputes Act, 1956, the tribunal adjudicates the disputes referred to it. The Court held that the reference encompassed all disputes emerging from the complaint, including the disputes underlying the interim-relief applications. It did not decide whether the tribunal had power to grant interim relief.

predicates.appeal_from_dismissal_of_interim_applica: A party appealed the dismissal of applications seeking interim relief from a statutory tribunal.
predicates.reference_covers_disputes_emerging_from_: The referring authority assigned the tribunal the disputes emerging from the complaint, and the applications concern those disputes.
predicates.complaint_sought_immediate_relief: The complaint described ongoing or imminent injury and sought immediate relief in connection with the dispute.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges dismissal of interim applications, the reference covers the disputes emerging from the complaint, and the complaint sought immediate relief, the tribunal must decide the applications on their merits.
